Known failures are the field failures the model is meant to reproduce (findings F-1, F-2, F-3). A new failure is a surprise and needs a look.
Test cases: D-L2P-01 D-L2P-02 D-L2P-03 D-L2P-04 D-L2P-05 D-L2P-06

How to review

  1. Banner. No new failures, and the known ones are the field failures?
  2. Each case: read the purpose and conditions before the plots; check the blue trace against the dashed limits.
  3. Remember the model. Averaged over a switching period: no ripple, no ringing, no device heating. It shows where the energy goes, not what the scope will show.

D-L2P-01 · Prediction for L2-OV-01: 0.5 A into VHigh, 60 V supply, 200 ohm bleed

The bench setup of L2-OV-01: low-side supply 24 V, VHigh lab supply 60 V (cannot sink), 200 ohm across VHigh, both legs' VHigh capacitors (276 uF). Current reference -0.5 A. Above 0.75 A the injected power exceeds what the resistor draws at 60 V, so VHigh settles above the set point at about sqrt(P*R).

1 · Test conditions and objectives

ControlPI current loop on iL, reference -0.5 A (negative: power into VHigh)
Low sidebattery (stiff source, series R_low), 24 V, 0.05 ohm
Supply on VHigh60 V, cannot sink current (lab supply), stays connected
Protectionnone (current firmware)
Self-supplyFeeder powered from VHigh (JP5001): PWM runs while VHigh > 8.9 V
Simulated300 ms, step 200 ns, computed in 7.3 s
ObjectiveWhat is checkedLimit
D-L2P-01.aPeak Vds(Q201) stays under the FET rating<= 150 V
D-L2P-01.bPeak |iL| stays under the L201/FET limit<= 40 A
D-L2P-01.cMargin to the 110 V absolute maximum of VHigh
D-L2P-01.dEvents and VHigh at the end of the run

D-L2P-05 · Prediction for L2-OV-02: 1.5 A into VHigh with the 200 ohm bleed, firmware stop at 80 V

At 1.5 A the injected power (36 W) would settle VHigh at about 85 V: the example's software stop (100 us control task) opens the leg at 80 V, then the bleed resistor brings VHigh back to the 60 V supply. Keeping the resistor means no charged capacitor is left at 80 V after the test.
